import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the event details. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def prepare_event_details(headline: str, summary: str, scheduled_date: str, additional_info: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- headline : str Title or name of the event. summary : str Comprehensive description of the event (may include multiple paragraphs). scheduled_date : str The scheduled date of the event. additional_info : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the organizer. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML for secure display of the event invitation. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is not a string. """ # Basic type validation to avoid accidental injection via non-string objects for name, value in [("headline", headline), ("summary", summary), ("scheduled_date", scheduled_date), ("additional_info", additional_info)]: if not isinstance(value, str): raise ValueError(f"{name!r} must be a string") # Escape all user-supplied content to prevent XSS escaped_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) escaped_summary = html.escape(summary, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") escaped_date = html.escape(scheduled_date, quote=True) escaped_info = html.escape(additional_info, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Format the sanitized content into the HTML template return INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=escaped_headline, event_description=escaped_summary, event_date=escaped_date, additional_notes=escaped_info )
